channel.title: Hastings Daily
channel.description: Local news for Hastings, St Leonards, Rye, Bexhill and Battle, three times a day.

item.title: Man found not guilty of sex offences on Camber Sands beach
item.description: A man from Kent has been found not guilty of a number of sexual offences against a woman on Camber Sands.

item.title: New management takes over 15th century Red Lion pub in Hooe
item.description: The Red Lion, a 15th century pub in Denbigh Road, Hooe, near Battle, has been taken over by new management.

item.title: Plans to reopen Marina Pavilion in St Leonards held up in dispute with council
item.description: The reopening of the Marina Pavilion on the St Leonards seafront has been delayed amid a row over council repair demands.

item.title: Storm power cuts threatened water supply to the Hastings area
item.description: Two water supply works serving the Hastings area shut down over the weekend after the storms knocked out local power, though taps kept running.

item.title: Fears of hungry children over half-term after holiday food vouchers axed
item.description: Families across East Sussex have not received automatic food vouchers for the October half term after the county council ended the school holiday scheme, raising fears that vulnerable children could go hungry.

item.title: Manhunt for escaped prisoner with links to Sussex
item.description: Police have launched a manhunt for a convicted prisoner with links to Sussex who escaped from a medical facility in South London on Friday.

item.title: Hastings Castle to get £288,500 from Historic England for repairs
item.description: Hastings Borough Council has been awarded £288,500 from Historic England's Heritage at Risk Capital Fund for repairs to Hastings Castle.

item.title: Hastings Philharmonic Choir to sing Schubert and Saint-Saëns
item.description: The Hastings Philharmonic Choir's next concert, Songs of Light, brings two choral masterpieces to All Saints Church in the Old Town on Saturday 7 November.

item.title: On this day, 1823: New town hall market opens in the High Street
item.description: On 25 October 1823, the new town hall in the High Street opened its ground floor to the market traders, with 14 stalls taking up their positions.

item.title: Bexhill empty shops plan opens for public consultation
item.description: Rother District Council has asked residents and businesses to have their say on a plan to tackle long-term empty shops in Bexhill.

item.title: Buses replace trains between Tonbridge and Wadhurst from Saturday
item.description: No trains will run between Tonbridge and Wadhurst from Saturday 24 October until Sunday 1 November, as Network Rail carries out major work on the Hastings line. Rail replacement buses will operate throughout, and the closure extends to Battle on the final day.

item.title: Hastings mother wins national road safety award
item.description: A Hastings mother has won a national award for her campaign to make the roads safer, following the death of her son in a road accident.

item.title: Police secure closure order for Hastings property
item.description: Officers from the Hastings Neighbourhood Policing Team have secured a Closure Order for a property in Cornwallis Terrace, Hastings.

item.title: Hastings Greens split over national 'Zionism is racism' vote
item.description: The chair of Hastings Greens, Justin Lee Wynne, resigned his post and cancelled his party membership on Friday, citing an internal dispute over alleged bullying and his 'deeply uncomfortable' reaction to the national party's October 4 conference vote declaring the party 'anti-Zionist' and labelling Zionism as racism, the Hastings Independent Press reported.

item.title: Alabama 3 acoustic show at St Leonard's Church
item.description: Alabama 3 are bringing their acoustic show to St Leonard's Church, St Leonards-on-Sea, on Saturday 14 November, the Hastings Independent Press reported.

item.title: Council's free business support pilot to visit Hastings Old Town and Rye high streets
item.description: A new free business support pilot will reach independent shops and businesses in selected East Sussex high streets, including Hastings Old Town and Rye, the county council said.

item.title: Hastings and Rye MP criticises Bayeux Tapestry ticket phone system
item.description: The MP for Hastings and Rye has criticised the phone line the British Museum set up for local residents to book tickets for the Bayeux tapestry exhibition.

item.title: West Hill Lift gets £531,000 from National Lottery Heritage Fund
item.description: The National Lottery Heritage Fund has offered £531,000 in development funding to Hastings Borough Council to secure the long-term future of the West Hill Lift, the Grade II listed lift that runs up the cliff from George Street to Hastings Castle.

item.title: Warm Homes Plan cuts would be 'terrible blunder', local energy service warns
item.description: A local energy advice service has warned that cuts to the government's Warm Homes Plan would be a 'terrible blunder' for households across East Sussex.

item.title: On this day, 1944: Hastings' secret evacuation plans revealed
item.description: On Saturday 21 October 1944, the Hastings and St Leonards Observer printed what the town had not been allowed to know during the war: the full story of the secret plans to evacuate the whole borough in the event of a German invasion.
